results.q: What happens when the broker does not answer a ping in time?
answer: This is handled in keepalive() (MQTTClient-C/src/MQTTClient.c:219): it checks `TimerIsExpired(&c->last_sent) || TimerIsExpired(&c->last_received)`, and when that is true it checks `c->ping_outstanding` (line 221); if true it sets `rc = FAILURE`; otherwise it calls TimerInit(), TimerCountdownMS(), MQTTSerialize_pingreq() and sets `int len = MQTTSerialize_pingreq(c->buf, c->buf_size)`; then it checks `len > 0 && (rc = sendPacket(c, len, &timer)) == SUCCESS` (SUCCESS = 0) (line 229); if true it sets `c->ping_outstanding = 1`.
TimerInit() sets `timer->end_time = (struct timeval){0, 0}` (line 22).
TimerCountdownMS() calls gettimeofday(&now, NULL) (line 37).

keepalive()'s caller cycle() checks `keepalive(c) != SUCCESS` (MQTTClient-C/src/MQTTClient.c:327) and then records it (`rc = FAILURE`) and later, where it tests `rc == SUCCESS` (line 333), when that is not true calls MQTTCloseSession().
cycle()'s caller MQTTYield() checks `cycle(c, &timer) < 0` (MQTTClient-C/src/MQTTClient.c:351) and then records it (`rc = FAILURE`).
cycle() is called by waitfor() inside a loop, which keeps retrying while `rc != packet_type && rc >= 0` (MQTTClient-C/src/MQTTClient.c:399).

results.q: What happens when an incoming packet is bigger than the read buffer?
answer: This is handled in readPacket() (MQTTClient-C/src/MQTTClient.c:127): it checks `rem_len > (c->readbuf_size - len)`, and when that is true it records it (`rc = BUFFER_OVERFLOW`) and jumps to `exit` (line 143), skipping the rest of readPacket().
Because it returns early, these do not happen in this case: TimerLeftMS(), TimerCountdown() — the previous values stay in place.

results.q: What happens when a message arrives on a topic that has no message handler?
answer: This is handled in MQTTSetMessageHandler() (MQTTClient-C/src/MQTTClient.c:495): it checks `messageHandler != NULL`, and when that is true it checks `rc == FAILURE` (FAILURE = -1) (line 496); then it repeats while `i < MAX_MESSAGE_HANDLERS` (line 498); then it checks `c->messageHandlers[i].topicFilter == NULL` (line 500); if true it sets `rc = SUCCESS`; then it checks `i < MAX_MESSAGE_HANDLERS` (MAX_MESSAGE_HANDLERS = 5) (line 507); if true it sets `c->messageHandlers[i].topicFilter = topicFilter`, `c->messageHandlers[i].fp = messageHandler`.

Consequence: deliverMessage() checks `c->messageHandlers[i].topicFilter != 0 && (MQTTPacket_equals(topicName, (char*)c->messageHandlers[i].topicFilter) || isTopicMatched((char*)c->messageHandlers[i].topicFilter, topicName))` (MQTTClient-C/src/MQTTClient.c:187); `c->messageHandlers[i].topicFilter != 0 && (MQTTPacket_equals(topicName, (char*)c->messageHandlers[i].topicFilter) || isTopicMatched((char*)c->messageHandlers[i].topicFilter, topicName))` depends on runtime values, so it may call NewMessageData() and may call messageArrived() and may call messageArrived2().

Consequence: deliverMessage() checks `c->messageHandlers[i].fp != NULL` (MQTTClient-C/src/MQTTClient.c:190); `c->messageHandlers[i].fp != NULL` depends on runtime values, so it may call NewMessageData() and may call messageArrived() and may call messageArrived2().

results.q: What happens when the broker rejects a subscription?
answer: This is handled in MQTTDeserialize_unsubscribe() (MQTTPacket/src/MQTTUnsubscribeServer.c:46): it checks `header.bits.type != UNSUBSCRIBE`, and when that is true it jumps to `exit` (line 67), skipping the rest of MQTTDeserialize_unsubscribe().
Because it returns early, these do not happen in this case: MQTTPacket_decodeBuf(), readInt(), readMQTTLenString() — the previous values stay in place.

results.q: What happens when MQTTPublish is called while the client is not connected?
answer: This is handled in MQTTPublish() (MQTTClient-C/src/MQTTClient.c:628): it checks `!c->isconnected`, and when that is true it jumps to `exit` (line 669), where it calls MQTTCloseSession(), skipping the rest of MQTTPublish().
Because it returns early, these do not happen in this case: TimerInit(), TimerCountdownMS(), getNextPacketId(), MQTTSerialize_publish() — the previous values stay in place.

results.q: What happens when the remaining length field of a packet is longer than four bytes?
answer: This is handled in MQTTPacket_decode() (MQTTPacket/src/MQTTPacket.c:67): it checks `++len > MAX_NO_OF_REMAINING_LENGTH_BYTES`, and when that is true it records it (`rc = MQTTPACKET_READ_ERROR`) and jumps to `exit` (line 78), skipping the rest of MQTTPacket_decode().
Because it returns early, these do not happen in this case: bufchar(), transport_getdata() — the previous values stay in place.

results.q: What happens when the buffer is too small to serialize a publish packet?
answer: This is handled in MQTTSerialize_publish() (MQTTPacket/src/MQTTSerializePublish.c:64): it checks `MQTTPacket_len(rem_len = MQTTSerialize_publishLength(qos, topicName, payloadlen)) > buflen`, and when that is true it records it (`rc = MQTTPACKET_BUFFER_TOO_SHORT`) and jumps to `exit` (line 88), skipping the rest of MQTTSerialize_publish().
Because it returns early, these do not happen in this case: writeChar(), MQTTPacket_encode(), writeMQTTString(), writeInt() — the previous values stay in place.

It is called by keepalive() at MQTTClient-C/src/MQTTClient.c:229, only when `c->keepAliveInterval == 0` is false, only when `TimerIsExpired(&c->last_sent) || TimerIsExpired(&c->last_received)` is true, only when `c->ping_outstanding` is false; cycle() at MQTTClient-C/src/MQTTClient.c:297, only when `MQTTDeserialize_publish(&msg.dup, &intQoS, &msg.retained, &msg.id, &topicName, (unsigned char**)&msg.payload, (int*)&msg.payloadlen, c->readbuf, c->readbuf_size) != 1` is false, only when `msg.qos != QOS0` is true (QOS0 = 0), only when `len <= 0` is false; cycle() at MQTTClient-C/src/MQTTClient.c:313, in the case `packet_type == PUBREC`, only when `MQTTDeserialize_ack(&type, &dup, &mypacketid, c->readbuf, c->readbuf_size) != 1` is false, only when `(len = MQTTSerialize_ack(c->buf, c->buf_size, (packet_type == PUBREC) ? results.q: Where does the topic name of a received message come from?
answer: MessageData.topicName (field, MQTTClient-C/src/MQTTClient.h:89).
It is assigned by `md->topicName = aTopicName` in NewMessageData() (MQTTClient-C/src/MQTTClient.c:24).
Tracing back further, the value originates at readMQTTLenString.mqttstring (parameter) and travels: MQTTDeserialize_publish() → cycle() → deliverMessage() → NewMessageData() → MessageData.topicName.

It is written here: `c->isconnected = 0` in MQTTClientInit() (MQTTClient-C/src/MQTTClient.c:70); `c->isconnected = 0` in MQTTCloseSession() (MQTTClient-C/src/MQTTClient.c:251); `c->isconnected = 1` in MQTTConnectWithResults() (MQTTClient-C/src/MQTTClient.c:456).

There is no `MQTTReconnect` in this code (none of its 1305 indexed symbols has that name). The closest names are __MQTT_LINUX_ (MQTTClient-C/src/linux/MQTTLinux.h:18), MQTT_CLIENT_H (MQTTClient-C/src/MQTTClient.h:20), MQTT_CONNECTION_ACCEPTED (MQTTPacket/src/MQTTConnect.h:25), described below.
__MQTT_LINUX_ is a constant (macro), defined in MQTTClient-C/src/linux/MQTTLinux.h:18.
Nothing in this code assigns __MQTT_LINUX_ after its declaration.
